react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics dataset strongly implicates tryptophan catabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway across four independent analytical paradigms. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as the top-ranked pathway with FDR 3.44e-15 and fold-enrichment 750.6, hitting 6 of 10 input metabolites (tryptamine, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, melatonin, L-tryptophan, serotonin). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 as rank 1 (p = 5.41e-09), with the identical six compounds mapped from the HMDB-resolved input list. Mummichog's empirical-compound m/z network also ranked Tryptophan metabolism first (p = 0.0033), capturing 7 metabolites including the decarboxylase-branch product alongside the classic kynurenine/serotonin intermediates. The RaMP Reactome layer additionally flagged REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) as rank 3 (FDR 3.59e-08), confirming that the treatment group modulates both the neuroactive and the NAD+-precursor arms of tryptophan degradation. Driver metabolites L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin form a coherent substrate-intermediate-product chain (TPH → TPH2, AANAT, ASMT), while 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid anchors the kynurenine branch that feeds into NAD+ biosynthesis. 4-Hydroxyretinoic acid, mapped to Vitamin A metabolism (rank 2, p = 0.082), and 3-aminopropanal (Histidine/Beta-Alanine metabolism, rank 2, p = 0.096) represent secondary signals below significance thresholds. The convergence across ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR) and m/z-network (Mummichog) paradigms provides robust evidence that the treatment primarily dysregulates tryptophan degradation, with downstream consequences for neuroactive serotonin/melatonin signalling and cellular NAD+ homeostasis.

MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 as rank 1 (p = 5.41e-09), with the identical six compounds mapped from the HMDB-resolved input list. Mummichog's empirical-compound m/z network also ranked Tryptophan metabolism first (p = 0.0033), capturing 7 metabolites including the decarboxylase-branch product alongside the classic kynurenine/serotonin intermediates. The RaMP Reactome layer additionally flagged REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) as rank 3 (FDR 3.59e-08), confirming that the treatment group modulates both the neuroactive and the NAD+-precursor arms of tryptophan degradation. Driver metabolites L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin form a coherent substrate-intermediate-product chain (TPH → TPH2, AANAT, ASMT), while 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid anchors the kynurenine branch that feeds into NAD+ biosynthesis. 4-Hydroxyretinoic acid, mapped to Vitamin A metabolism (rank 2, p = 0.082), and 3-aminopropanal (Histidine/Beta-Alanine metabolism, rank 2, p = 0.096) represent secondary signals below significance thresholds. The convergence across ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR) and m/z-network (Mummichog) paradigms provides robust evidence that the treatment primarily dysregulates tryptophan degradation, with downstream consequences for neuroactive serotonin/melatonin signalling and cellular NAD+ homeostasis.
